what_you_can_do: Convert RMB soon after it arrives
what_it_changes: The currency clock starts on the day the RMB is received, so little gain or loss has time to build. RMB received in the latest months shows almost none.
in_favour: Removes most of the currency tax on new money such as a recent sale or recent pay.
against: Does nothing for RMB that has already been held through a rate move.

what_you_can_do: Spread the conversion over two tax years
what_it_changes: Each conversion is its own transaction, taxed in the year it happens, so the gain is divided between two returns.
in_favour: Can keep the gain in a lower bracket in each year, and under the 3.8% threshold.
against: The rate can move against you while you wait, and the bank charges for each wire.

what_you_can_do: Choose the withdrawal method with care, once
what_it_changes: First in first out, last in first out and pro rata give different gains for a part-conversion; when the account is emptied the total is the same.
in_favour: Decides which year carries the gain. In the personal box it can also change the total taxed, because a tranche that shows a loss is simply lost.
against: The choice binds later years and every foreign-currency account. Highest-cost-first is not allowed.

what_you_can_do: Establish which box the money is in, with papers
what_it_changes: The box sets the rate (ordinary or capital) and decides whether a loss counts.
in_favour: With a gain on RMB held over a year, the personal box gives the lower capital rates, including 0% under the zero-rate amount. With a loss, the investment box makes it an ordinary loss instead of a lost one.
against: The box follows the facts; it is not a choice. The official texts do not place a savings balance in either one.

what_you_can_do: Convert in a year when other income is low
what_it_changes: A long-term capital gain is taxed at 0% while taxable income stays within the zero-rate amount: $49,450 single, $98,900 joint in 2026.
in_favour: A gain in the personal box can then cost nothing in federal tax.
against: Applies only to a long-term capital gain; an ordinary gain is taxed from the first bracket upward.

what_you_can_do: Keep the money in RMB for now
what_it_changes: No gain or loss is recognized until the RMB is sold or spent; moving it between RMB deposits does not count.
in_favour: Defers the tax and keeps the choice of year open.
against: The gain keeps moving with the rate, the money stays in China, and buying property or investments with it is itself a taxable disposal.

what_you_can_do: Know whether the money was inherited or given
what_it_changes: Inherited RMB starts again at its value on the date of death; gifted RMB keeps the giver's cost.
in_favour: For inherited money only the movement since the death counts.
against: This is a fact to prove, not a choice. For a gift from someone who is not a U.S. taxpayer the texts read do not say how the dollar cost is measured.

what_you_can_do: Do not route the conversion through another person or a company
what_it_changes: Nothing: the regulation lets the IRS treat a transaction or a series of transactions as a section 988 transaction where its effect is to avoid the section. The regulation's example is currency placed in a new company whose shares are then sold.
against: Adds risk without changing the gain. The Chinese rules on using someone else's quota are on the dashboard's Methods page.
